authority.legal_name: Ministry of Transportation and Telecommunications (MTT/MOTC), Kingdom of Bahrain

mandate.summary: MOTC develops and regulates Bahrain's integrated land, sea, and air transport networks. Sea transport master-planning sits squarely inside its remit, alongside the Bahrain Metro and modernization of public transport.
current_priorities: Modernize and integrate public transport (bus network, planned Bahrain Metro)
Develop master plans for integrated land, sea and air networks
Grow Bahrain as a regional maritime and logistics hub

policy_targets.vision: Bahrain Economic Vision 2030 — sustainable, diversified economy with modern infrastructure
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission marine transport mode contributes directly to the 2035 interim cut and the 2060 net-zero target while modernizing public transport under Vision 2030.

precedent.headline: Bahrain has already committed to water as public transport.

existing_water_taxi.name: Bahrain Water Taxi Project
existing_water_taxi.vessels: Locally manufactured, air-conditioned, Wi-Fi, restrooms, up to ~28 passengers
existing_water_taxi.proof_stat: Reported ~4 minutes on water vs ~15 minutes by road on a Manama–Muharraq leg (~75% time saving at peak).

qatar_bahrain_ferry.note: First-ever direct international passenger sea route in the Gulf; booking via Masar app; opened to non-GCC travellers. Makes the Bahrain<->Qatar corridor a live bilateral reality, not a roadmap aspiration.
qatar_bahrain_ferry.variant_source: One report cites Khalifa bin Salman Port / ~50 min; Al-Ruwais<->Sa'ada Marina is the dominant citation.

king_fahd_causeway.link: Bahrain <-> Al Khobar/Dammam, KSA Eastern Province
king_fahd_causeway.stat: ~33 million crossings per year; congested at peaks
king_fahd_causeway.relevance: A fast cross-Gulf marine link offers causeway-peak relief — a public-good framing the authority already understands.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is not introducing a novelty. MOTC already runs a water taxi and just opened an international ferry. Navier is the vessel/technology upgrade that lets the national water-transport mode scale: foiling hulls are faster, near-silent, low-wake, zero-emission, weather-resilient, and longer-range than the current 28-pax displacement boats — enough to serve the full archipelago and credible cross-Gulf relief corridors.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real berths/marinas during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Inner core mirrors the six live water-taxi stations; archipelago extension adds real, water-accessible developments.

domestic_pairs.rationale: Live water-taxi leg today; foiling cuts the crossing further and runs all-weather. Anchor proof corridor.
Dense Manama business core to Amwaj residential/leisure island; today a causeway road loop.
Bahrain Bay to the large Diyar development; direct across sheltered water vs causeway detour.
Waterside airport access from the Manama core, bypassing causeway road congestion.
Southern industrial/residential Sitra to the business core.
Manama to the far-south Durrat resort/residential complex; long sheltered east-coast run.
Eco/leisure outer-island access (seasonal); demonstrates archipelago reach.

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. One is already a live bilateral reality; the other is a recognized congestion-relief corridor. Neither leads the proposal.

links.note: Mirrors the operating Bahrain<->Qatar passenger ferry (Nov 2025). A foiling service would cut the 70-80 min crossing materially.
King Fahd Causeway peak relief; subject to bilateral operating review. Routing must use the causeway navigation channel.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings. Hand-curated waypoints required where coastline, causeways, reefs or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: Manama and Muharraq are joined by multiple causeways/bridges (Shaikh Hamad, Shaikh Isa bin Salman, Shaikh Khalifa). Inner legs must route around the open water north/east of the causeways or through marked bridge navigation spans — never straight across a causeway.
Any Bahrain<->KSA leg must pass through the marked navigation channel at the causeway (near Passport Island), not over the embankment.
Legs to/from Sitra must follow the dredged channels, not cross the Sitra causeway.
West-coast and far-south waters are shallow with reef/sabkha flats; keep geometry in charted deeper channels east of the main islands.
These are reclaimed developments served by dredged approach channels; snap entries to the channel mouths, not the reclaimed edge.
